Candidate_refuter: Multi-expert learning to defer (softmax / OvA surrogates, conformal expert subset)
Citation: R. Verma, D. Barrejon, E. Nalisnick, 'Learning to Defer to Multiple Experts: Consistent Surrogate Losses, Confidence Calibration, and Conformal Ensembles', AISTATS 2023, PMLR 206:11415-11434.
Exact_capability: Learns, for each of J named experts, an estimate of P(m_j = y | x): the probability that expert j predicts the label correctly FOR THE SPECIFIC INPUT x; defers to a selected expert or expert subset.
What_it_matches: Selects among differentiated experts; conditions the selection on the specific instance rather than on a fixed per-expert average; models per-expert competence explicitly; supplies consistency and calibration theory.
What_it_does_not_match: No representation of authority, mandate or decision rights; the expert panel is fixed and known in advance; requires per-expert ground-truth outcome labels to fit; the unit is a prediction with one true label, not a contested claim admitting several defensible readings; no attention-budget or selective-risk evaluation of the routing decision itself.
Evidence: Abstract verified verbatim on the PMLR page: 'we study the frameworks ability to estimate P( m_j = y | x ), the probability that the jth expert will correctly predict the label for x'.
Effect_on_proposal: Forces correction of the Section 2.6 sentence characterising multi-expert deferral as conditioning on 'an aggregate competence profile over a task distribution'. That characterisation is inaccurate. GAP-1 must be restated as the competence-AND-authority conjunction, conceding instance-conditional competence to this line of work.
Source_verified: YES - PMLR v206 proceedings page (proceedings.mlr.press/v206/verma23a.html); page range matches proposal reference [60] exactly

Candidate_refuter: Two-stage learning to defer with multiple experts
Citation: A. Mao, C. Mohri, M. Mohri, Y. Zhong, 'Two-Stage Learning to Defer with Multiple Experts', Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36, 2023.
Exact_capability: Two-stage formulation: a predictor is trained first, then a deferral/routing function selects among multiple experts, with realizable H-consistency guarantees.
What_it_matches: Routes to one of several differentiated experts; separates the routing decision from the base predictor, which is architecturally the same separation the proposal proposes for its review policy.
What_it_does_not_match: Expert differentiation is by cost and accuracy only; no authority, mandate, scope or eligibility construct; still label-supervised; no per-claim authority test.
Evidence: Venue, authorship and year confirmed against the NeurIPS 2023 proceedings record (proceedings.neurips.cc, paper hash 0b17d256cf1fe1cc084922a8c6b565b7).
Effect_on_proposal: Reinforces the same narrowing as Verma et al. The page range 3578-3606 given in reference [61] was not independently confirmed and should be checked against the printed proceedings.
Source_verified: PARTIAL - venue/authors/year verified via NeurIPS proceedings; page range unconfirmed

Candidate_refuter: Exact algorithms for learning to defer to a single human
Citation: H. Mozannar, H. Lang, D. Wei, P. Sattigeri, S. Das, D. Sontag, 'Who Should Predict? Exact Algorithms for Learning to Defer to Humans', AISTATS 2023, PMLR 206:10520-10545.

What_it_matches: Formalises the who-decides question and characterises the realisable optimum; the strongest available comparator for any routing claim.
What_it_does_not_match: One undifferentiated human; no selection among reviewers at all, therefore neither claim-specific competence nor authority.
Evidence: Cited in the proposal as [37]; venue and volume consistent with the AISTATS 2023 PMLR 206 volume that also contains Verma et al.
Effect_on_proposal: No change required. The proposal already characterises single-expert deferral correctly.
Source_verified: PARTIAL - PMLR v206 volume confirmed; individual page range not separately fetched

Candidate_refuter: Workflow resource patterns: capability-based distribution, authorisation, separation of duties
Citation: N. Russell, W. M. P. van der Aalst, A. H. M. ter Hofstede, D. Edmond, 'Workflow Resource Patterns: Identification, Representation and Tool Support', CAiSE 2005, LNCS 3520, pp. 216-232, doi:10.1007/11431855_16.
Exact_capability: A catalogue of resource patterns for allocating a work item to a participant, including Role-Based Distribution, Capability-Based Distribution, Organisational Distribution, Authorisation, Separation of Duties, Retain Familiar and History-Based Distribution.
What_it_matches: The single closest structural match to GAP-1 found anywhere in this audit: ONE framework represents BOTH a capability requirement on the participant AND an authorisation constraint on who may execute that specific work item, evaluated per work item.
What_it_does_not_match: Capability is a DECLARED, largely static attribute matched by predicate satisfaction, not a competence ASSESSED from evidence for the specific item; the unit is a process work item with a defined completion criterion, not a contested claim with several defensible readings; the catalogue is a design and expressiveness vocabulary with tool support, not an evaluated routing policy, and reports no accuracy, attention-budget or selective-risk outcome.
Evidence: Pattern names and the joint capability-plus-authorisation coverage confirmed via the Springer chapter record and the workflowpatterns.com documentation; DOI, pages 216-232 and year 2005 confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Materially narrows GAP-1. The proposal cannot claim that no reviewed formulation represents competence and authority together; it must claim that none represents ASSESSED, claim-specific competence together with authority, and that none has been evaluated as a routing policy under a matched attention budget. This paper must be cited.
Source_verified: YES - Crossref DOI 10.1007/11431855_16, pages 216-232, 2005 (note: the Crossref container-title field is corrupted to an unrelated fluid-mechanics series; LNCS 3520 / CAiSE 2005 is the true venue per the Springer record)

Candidate_refuter: Authorisation constraints in workflow management systems
Citation: E. Bertino, E. Ferrari, V. Atluri, 'The specification and enforcement of authorization constraints in workflow management systems', ACM Transactions on Information and System Security 2(1):65-104, 1999, doi:10.1145/300830.300837.
Exact_capability: A logic-based language for specifying, and an algorithm for enforcing, role and user authorisation constraints on individual workflow tasks, including static and dynamic separation of duty and binding of duty.
What_it_matches: Authority to act on a specific task is a first-class, formally enforced object, decided per task and per actor - exactly the 'authority to decide this item' half of GAP-1, with an enforcement mechanism.
What_it_does_not_match: Contains no competence, skill or accuracy model whatsoever; authorisation is orthogonal to whether the authorised actor is any good at the task; no notion of contested interpretation.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 65-104 and year 1999 confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Supplies the authority half in mature formal form. GAP-1 must concede that authority modelling is a solved, long-standing problem in this literature, and locate its own contribution in the joint, assessed-competence-conditioned decision.

Candidate_refuter: Resource assignment languages for business processes (RAL / RALph)
Citation: C. Cabanillas et al., 'RALph: A Graphical Notation for Resource Assignments in Business Processes', CAiSE 2015, LNCS, pp. 53-68, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-19069-3_4; and 'RAL: A High-Level User-Oriented Resource Assignment Language for Business Processes', LNBIP, pp. 50-61, doi:10.1007/978-3-642-28108-2_5.
Exact_capability: A notation and formal language for expressing which resources may be assigned to an activity, in terms of organisational position, role, capability, and history-based and duty-separation conditions.
What_it_matches: Expresses capability requirements and organisational-position (authority-like) requirements in one assignment expression, resolvable against an organisational model.
What_it_does_not_match: Assignment conditions are declarative constraints over declared organisational attributes; no assessment of competence for the specific instance; no evaluation as a decision policy against outcomes; the unit is an activity, not a claim.
Evidence: Both DOIs, page ranges and years confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Must be cited as part of the conceded competence-plus-authority representation capability of BPM. Strengthens the need to reword GAP-1 around ASSESSED competence.

Citation: M. Arias, E. Rojas, J. Munoz-Gama, M. Sepulveda, 'A Framework for Recommending Resource Allocation Based on Process Mining', BPM Workshops, LNBIP, pp. 458-470, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-42887-1_37.
Exact_capability: Derives resource-allocation recommendations from historical event-log evidence of how resources actually performed on comparable work items.
What_it_matches: The nearest thing in BPM to ASSESSED rather than declared competence: the allocation signal is estimated from observed past performance, per activity type.
What_it_does_not_match: Competence is estimated at the level of activity type and resource, not for one contested claim; authority is not jointly modelled in the recommendation; no authority-competence separation; recommends rather than governs.
Evidence: DOI, pages 458-470 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Partially closes the 'BPM has no assessed competence' escape route. GAP-1's residual must therefore rest on the JOINT decision, the claim-level unit and budgeted evaluation - not on the absence of assessed competence in BPM.

Candidate_refuter: Systematic literature study of resource allocation in business process executions
Citation: L. Pufahl, F. Stiehle, S. Ihde, M. Weske, I. Weber, 'Resource allocation in business process executions - A systematic literature study', Information Systems, 2025, art. 102541, doi:10.1016/j.is.2025.102541.
Exact_capability: Systematic review of 61 primary studies (1995-2023) on system-initiated resource allocation, classifying allocation goals, inputs, criteria and methods.
What_it_matches: An authoritative, current map of exactly the literature the proposal names as its likeliest refuter; establishes what that field does and does not do without relying on the candidate's own reading of it.
What_it_does_not_match: Reports that reviewed approaches are predominantly rule-based and process-oriented, mostly 1-to-1 allocations, and explicitly calls for future work on evidence-oriented allocation methods with greater adaptability and on comparative benchmarking - that is, the field's own systematic review identifies the absence of evidence-oriented allocation and of comparative evaluation.
Evidence: Title, authors, journal, year and DOI confirmed via Crossref and OpenAlex; scope (61 primary studies, 1995-2023) and the rule-based / process-oriented / evidence-oriented-future-work findings taken from the abstract via OpenAlex.
Effect_on_proposal: The strongest single piece of evidence that GAP-1 survives as NARROWED rather than refuted: the adjacent literature's own recent systematic review reports that its allocation methods are not evidence-oriented and are not comparatively benchmarked. Must be cited in Section 2.6 in place of the present bare declaration that BPM 'has not been searched'.

Candidate_refuter: Systematic mapping of human resource allocation in BPM and process mining
Citation: M. Arias, R. Saavedra, M. R. Marques, J. Munoz-Gama, M. Sepulveda, 'Human resource allocation in business process management and process mining: A systematic mapping study', Management Decision 56(2):376-405, 2018, doi:10.1108/md-05-2017-0476.
Exact_capability: Mapping study producing a taxonomy of human-resource allocation criteria over task and resource attributes.
What_it_matches: Supplies the established criteria taxonomy against which the proposal's eight declared routing signals should be positioned rather than presented as new.
What_it_does_not_match: A mapping study, not an approach; does not itself route or evaluate; no authority-competence separation.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 376-405 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Study 1's signal set should be crosswalked against this taxonomy so the proposal's signals are shown to be a positioned selection rather than an invention.

Candidate_refuter: Deadline-based escalation in process-aware information systems
Citation: W. M. P. van der Aalst, M. Rosemann, M. Dumas, 'Deadline-based escalation in process-aware information systems', Decision Support Systems 43(2):492-511, 2007, doi:10.1016/j.dss.2006.11.005.
Exact_capability: Formalises escalation mechanisms triggered when a work item breaches a deadline, including reassignment to different resources.
What_it_matches: Escalation as a governed, specified state transition rather than an ad-hoc handoff - the closest BPM analogue to the proposal's escalation actions.
What_it_does_not_match: The trigger is a temporal deadline, not evidence quality, uncertainty, consequence or reviewer fit; target selection is not competence-assessed.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 492-511 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Cite as the escalation-policy comparator for Study 1's six actions.

Candidate_refuter: Statutory requirement that human overseers hold competence AND authority
Citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 26(2).
Exact_capability: Legal obligation on deployers of high-risk AI systems: 'Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.'
What_it_matches: Explicitly conjoins competence AND authority as joint requirements on a human overseer - the exact pair GAP-1 is built on. The conjunction is therefore already a stated normative requirement in binding regulation.
What_it_does_not_match: Imposes a requirement on the assignment of oversight duty at role and deployment level; supplies no mechanism, no per-claim selection procedure, no competence assessment method and no evaluation. It states that the conjunction must hold, not how to decide it for one contested claim.
Evidence: Article 26(2) text quoted verbatim from the consolidated article text (artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/26); regulation identifier Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
Effect_on_proposal: Significant for the claim audit. The proposal must not present the competence-plus-authority conjunction as conceptually novel, because binding EU regulation already requires it. Novelty must be relocated to the OPERATIONALISATION: a per-claim, evidence-conditioned, budgeted routing policy that has been evaluated. This strengthens the motivation while removing an overclaim.
Source_verified: YES - consolidated Article 26 text; the candidate should re-verify against the EUR-Lex Official Journal text before citing

Citation: J. Fugener, J. Grahl, A. Gupta, W. Ketter, 'Cognitive Challenges in Human-Artificial Intelligence Collaboration: Investigating the Path Toward Productive Delegation', Information Systems Research 33(2):678-696, 2022, doi:10.1287/isre.2021.1079.
Exact_capability: Experimental study of who should delegate to whom between a human and an AI, and of humans' metacognitive inability to judge their own relative competence.
What_it_matches: Directly evidences that self-assessed competence is an unreliable routing signal, which supports designing routing as a system decision rather than a reviewer's choice.
What_it_does_not_match: Two-party delegation between one human and one model; no selection among differentiated reviewers; no authority; the unit is a prediction task.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 678-696 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Add to Section 2.3 as empirical support for system-initiated rather than self-selected review.

Candidate_refuter: Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations
Citation: T. Clark, P. N. Ciccarese, C. A. Goble, 'Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications', Journal of Biomedical Semantics 5:28, 2014, doi:10.1186/2041-1480-5-28.
Exact_capability: An OWL 2 / RDF model whose unit of record is a single CLAIM, carrying its attribution, supporting data, methods and materials, the argument connecting evidence to the claim, and explicitly represented challenges and opposition.
What_it_matches: Claim-level unit; reasoning-level content (argument and evidence, not only the conclusion); attribution to an agent; provenance; and RETAINED DISAGREEMENT as a first-class relation - the model is explicitly designed to support challenge and disagreement rather than collapse to one verdict. The closest identified match to the SQ2 record, and absent from the anchor set.
What_it_does_not_match: No validity SCOPE on the claim; no competence or authority attached to the claiming agent beyond identity attribution; no lifecycle - no expiry, no supersession condition, no revocation semantics, no version binding to a specific artefact version; and no evaluation of reconstructability or capture cost.
Evidence: Title, authors, journal, article number, year and DOI confirmed via Crossref and OpenAlex. Abstract obtained via OpenAlex: the model provides statements with attribution, supports 'challenge and disagreement', and maximal forms include 'all relevant evidence, interpretations, discussions, challenges brought forward or opposition'.
Effect_on_proposal: Requires the Section 2.4 sentence 'No record format combines reasoning-level content, scope, authority, retained disagreement, and a lifecycle at claim level' to be narrowed. Reasoning-level content plus retained disagreement plus provenance at claim level ALREADY EXISTS. The residual is scope, authority/competence and lifecycle. This paper must be cited.

Citation: P. Groth, A. Gibson, J. Velterop, 'The anatomy of a nanopublication', Information Services and Use 30(1-2):51-56, 2010, doi:10.3233/isu-2010-0613.
Exact_capability: A minimal citable unit consisting of an assertion plus its provenance plus publication information, immutable and individually identified.
What_it_matches: Claim-level unit with provenance and version-exact identity by construction; individually addressable and citable, which is the version-binding property SQ2 requires.
What_it_does_not_match: The assertion is a factual statement, not a governed human judgment; no rationale or argument structure (that is what micropublications add); no competence or authority; no expiry or lapse condition; retraction is an ecosystem convention rather than a modelled lifecycle state.
Evidence: Title, authors, journal, volume, pages 51-56, year and DOI confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Concede version-exact claim-level provenance as existing prior art. Cite alongside micropublications.

Citation: J. Singh, J. Cobbe, C. Norval, 'Decision Provenance: Harnessing Data Flow for Accountable Systems', IEEE Access 7:6562-6574, 2019, doi:10.1109/access.2018.2887201.
Exact_capability: Applies provenance methods specifically to DECISIONS in data-driven systems, to make the decision pipeline inspectable and accountable across system boundaries.
What_it_matches: Makes the same move SQ2 makes - from data lineage to decision accountability - and is framed around legal accountability and redress.
What_it_does_not_match: Records how a decision was produced; does not represent a human judgment as a reusable governed object with scope, authority, competence or a lapse condition; no adjudication of conflicting qualified judgments.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 6562-6574 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Must be cited. It occupies the conceptual space between PROV-DM [47] and SQ2 and is currently missing from the anchor set, which weakens the claim that the step from provenance to governed judgment is unmade.

Citation: J. Doyle, 'A truth maintenance system', Artificial Intelligence 12(3):231-272, 1979, doi:10.1016/0004-3702(79)90008-0.
Exact_capability: Maintains justifications for each stored belief and retracts beliefs automatically when their supporting justifications are withdrawn (dependency-directed backtracking).
What_it_matches: Supplies the assertion-lifecycle machinery SQ2 asks for: an assertion holds only while its support holds, and loses status automatically when support is withdrawn. This is a REASON-CONDITIONED lapse mechanism, which the proposal states provenance lacks.
What_it_does_not_match: Support is a logical dependency on other beliefs, not an external validity condition such as a changed guideline, an expiry date or a revoked mandate; no human agent, competence, authority or disagreement; no rationale intended for human consumption.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 231-272 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: The proposal already names truth maintenance as an exposed area; this audit confirms the exposure is real. The 'consequence obliging an invalidated judgment to stop influencing decisions' that Section 2.4 says provenance lacks is exactly what a TMS provides. Section 2.4 must concede this and relocate the residual to human-authored, authority-bearing judgments.

Citation: J. de Kleer, 'An assumption-based TMS', Artificial Intelligence 28(2):127-162, 1986, doi:10.1016/0004-3702(86)90080-9.
Exact_capability: Maintains multiple simultaneous, mutually inconsistent contexts, each labelled by the assumption set under which it holds.
What_it_matches: Represents conflicting conclusions concurrently WITHOUT collapsing them to one verdict, each with the conditions under which it holds - structurally the retained-disagreement-plus-scope combination SQ2 asks for.
What_it_does_not_match: Assumptions are propositional, not organisational scope or authority; no human attribution; no expiry or revocation by mandate.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 127-162 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Strengthens the narrowing of GAP-2's retained-disagreement and scope elements. Cite as the formal predecessor for scoped, conflicting assertions.

Citation: C. E. Alchourron, P. Gardenfors, D. Makinson, 'On the logic of theory change: Partial meet contraction and revision functions', Journal of Symbolic Logic 50(2):510-530, 1985, doi:10.2307/2274239.
Exact_capability: Axiomatic theory of how a belief set should change under expansion, contraction and revision, with rationality postulates and an epistemic-entrenchment ordering over which beliefs yield first.
What_it_matches: Supplies a principled account of WHICH assertion should give way when a stored commitment conflicts with new information - the normative core of supersession.
What_it_does_not_match: Set-theoretic and agent-neutral; no provenance, attribution, scope, authority or time; not a record format, and never evaluated as a capture mechanism.
Evidence: DOI 10.2307/2274239, journal, volume, pages 510-530 and year 1985 confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Cite as the normative predecessor for supersession. Enters via the documented pre-2015 snowballing exception.

Citation: G. Flouris, D. Manakanatas, H. Kondylakis, D. Plexousakis, G. Antoniou, 'Ontology change: classification and survey', The Knowledge Engineering Review 23(2):117-152, 2008, doi:10.1017/s0269888908001367; F. Zablith et al., 'Ontology evolution: a process-centric survey', The Knowledge Engineering Review, doi:10.1017/s0269888913000349.
Exact_capability: Surveys of how a knowledge structure is versioned, changed and kept consistent over time, including change classification, versioning and evolution processes.
What_it_matches: Establishes versioning and change management over stored knowledge as a mature research area with an explicit process view - covering the version-binding and supersession elements of SQ2.
What_it_does_not_match: Operates on schema and ontology artefacts, not on individual human judgments; no competence, authority, disagreement or per-assertion expiry keyed to a governing policy.
Evidence: Both DOIs, the 2008 volume and pages 117-152, and the process-centric survey record confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Cite as the versioning and supersession predecessor. Note the Zablith issue year (KER vol. 30) versus the Crossref online-first year when citing.

Citation: C. Gutierrez, C. A. Hurtado, A. Vaisman, 'Introducing Time into RDF', IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering 19(2):207-218, 2007, doi:10.1109/tkde.2007.34.
Exact_capability: Adds temporal validity to RDF assertions so that a statement holds only over a stated time interval, with semantics and entailment for temporal graphs.
What_it_matches: A lifecycle state able to LAPSE ON A STATED CONDITION at assertion level - one of the two findings the proposal itself declares would remove the need for Study 2.
What_it_does_not_match: The lapse condition is strictly a time interval; it cannot express 'lapses when the guideline changes', 'lapses when the mandate is withdrawn' or 'lapses when challenged by a more authorised reviewer'; and it carries no rationale, competence, authority or disagreement.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 207-218 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Directly engages SQ2's second stated refutation condition and must be addressed head-on. It satisfies that condition under a time-only reading of 'stated condition'. The proposal should tighten the refutation condition to a non-temporal, policy-or-evidence-keyed lapse condition; otherwise temporal RDF arguably meets it as written.

Citation: A. Uma, T. Fornaciari, D. Hovy, S. Paun, B. Plank, M. Poesio, 'Learning from Disagreement: A Survey', Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 72:1385-1470, 2021, doi:10.1613/jair.1.12752.
Exact_capability: Survey of methods that preserve and learn from disagreement among qualified annotators instead of aggregating to a single gold label.
What_it_matches: Establishes preserved disagreement as a mature, surveyed research area, well beyond the single position the proposal cites via crowd truth [50].
What_it_does_not_match: Concerns label distributions for model training; no per-judgment record with scope, authority or lifecycle; adjudication to an authoritative verdict is precisely what it avoids.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 1385-1470 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Section 2.4 currently rests the disagreement point on one 2015 AI Magazine article. Citing this survey and Davani et al. materially strengthens the section and removes an under-evidencing risk.

Citation: A. M. Davani, M. Diaz, V. Prabhakaran, 'Dealing with Disagreements: Looking Beyond the Majority Vote in Subjective Annotations', Transactions of the ACL 10:92-110, 2022, doi:10.1162/tacl_a_00449.

What_it_matches: Retains per-person judgments as distinct, attributable objects - the identity-preserving half of retained disagreement.

Citation: A. MacLean, R. M. Young, V. M. E. Bellotti, T. P. Moran, 'Questions, Options, and Criteria: Elements of Design Space Analysis', Human-Computer Interaction 6(3-4):201-250, 1991, doi:10.1207/s15327051hci0603&4_2.
Exact_capability: A representation capturing, for each design question, the options considered and the criteria by which they were assessed.
What_it_matches: Captures reasoning structure and the alternatives NOT chosen, at the level of an individual question - close to the proposal's claim-level rationale requirement, and it records why rejected readings were rejected.
What_it_does_not_match: No authority, competence, provenance binding to artefact versions, expiry or revocation; never evaluated for blind reconstructability or capture cost; a design-time artefact rather than a governed operational record.

Effect_on_proposal: Design rationale is an entire predecessor literature for SQ2 that the anchor set omits. Its omission is a genuine coverage gap in Chapter 2, not merely a missing citation.

Candidate_refuter: Issue-based rationale capture with retained positions and arguments
Citation: J. Conklin, M. L. Begeman, 'gIBIS: a hypertext tool for exploratory policy discussion', ACM Transactions on Information Systems 6(4):303-331, 1988, doi:10.1145/58566.59297.

Candidate_refuter: Architectural design decisions as first-class records
Citation: A. Jansen, J. Bosch, 'Software Architecture as a Set of Architectural Design Decisions', WICSA 2005, pp. 109-120, doi:10.1109/wicsa.2005.61; J. Tyree, A. Akerman, 'Architecture Decisions: Demystifying Architecture', IEEE Software 22(2):19-27, 2005, doi:10.1109/ms.2005.27.
Exact_capability: Treats each design decision as a persistent, first-class record carrying rationale, considered alternatives, assumptions, constraints and consequences; Tyree and Akerman give an explicit decision-record template.
What_it_matches: A decision record with rationale, alternatives and a stated scope of applicability, retained for later readers - a direct software-engineering predecessor for the SQ2 record, including the notion that a decision can later be superseded.
What_it_does_not_match: No claim-level binding to an artefact version, no competence or authority field, no expiry condition, no adjudication of conflicting qualified judgments, and no evaluated reconstructability.
Evidence: Both DOIs, pages and the 2005 year confirmed via Crossref.

Candidate_refuter: Compiling user corrections into runtime enforcement
Citation: Y. Zhou et al., 'Getting Better at Working With You: Compiling User Corrections into Runtime Enforcement for Coding Agents', arXiv:2606.13174, submitted 11 June 2026.
Exact_capability: Mines user corrections from chat, rewrites them as atomic rules, and compiles them into runtime checks that must pass before an agent completes later tasks.
What_it_matches: Demonstrates empirically that a remembered correction does not become compliance without an enforcement mechanism, and that compiled enforcement reduces held-out violation substantially - the enforcement-consequence element SQ2 requires.
What_it_does_not_match: Rules are derived automatically from corrections rather than authored as governed human judgments; no scope, authority, competence, retained disagreement, provenance binding or lifecycle; not peer reviewed.
Evidence: arXiv identifier, title, full author list, submission date 11 June 2026 and abstract confirmed on the arXiv abstract page; no peer-reviewed venue is stated.
Effect_on_proposal: Proposal reference [52] already marks this as a preprint and reads it as such - correct handling. Must remain Tier C and must not support any absence claim.
Source_verified: YES - arXiv abstract page; TIER C PREPRINT, not peer reviewed

Citation: D. Leake, M. Whitehead, 'Case Provenance: The Value of Remembering Case Sources', ICCBR 2007, LNCS, pp. 194-208, doi:10.1007/978-3-540-74141-1_14.
Exact_capability: Records where each stored case came from and uses that provenance to inform later retrieval and case-base maintenance decisions.
What_it_matches: Combines case-level provenance with a decision about the later USE of a stored case - the closest CBR predecessor to a governed reuse decision, and absent from the anchor set.
What_it_does_not_match: Provenance informs competence and maintenance of the store; it does not decide whether one stored judgment may act in one specific later context under someone's authority, and applies no authorisation, currency or target-evidence test.
Evidence: DOI, pages 194-208 and year 2007 confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Must be cited. It sits between Aamodt and Plaza [53] and Smyth and Keane [54], and narrows the claim that CBR maintenance decides only whole-store competence.

Citation: D. B. Leake, D. C. Wilson, 'Categorizing case-base maintenance: Dimensions and directions', EWCBR 1998, LNCS, pp. 196-207, doi:10.1007/bfb0056333.
Exact_capability: A framework classifying case-base maintenance policies by what is revised, when, how it is triggered and on what data.
What_it_matches: Supplies the established vocabulary for retention and revision policies over stored experience, against which SQ2 and SQ3 retention decisions should be positioned.
What_it_does_not_match: Maintenance operates over the store to preserve aggregate competence; it does not license or refuse an individual reuse event, and has no authorisation or target-context test.
Evidence: DOI, pages 196-207 and year 1998 confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Cite alongside [54] so the retention-policy comparator is the maintenance literature as a whole rather than a single 1995 paper.

Citation: R. Weber, D. W. Aha, I. Becerra-Fernandez, 'Intelligent lessons learned systems', Expert Systems with Applications 20(1):17-34, 2001, doi:10.1016/s0957-4174(00)00046-4.
Exact_capability: Surveys organisational lessons-learned systems and the process by which a recorded lesson is collected, verified, stored, disseminated and applied in later work.
What_it_matches: The lesson lifecycle it describes includes explicit VERIFICATION and RE-USE steps, and the survey's central finding is that lessons fail to influence later decisions unless delivery is embedded in the decision process - closely parallel to the proposal's enforcement-consequence argument for SQ2 and SQ3.
What_it_does_not_match: Lessons are organisation-level narrative records, not claim-level judgments; no authority binding, no expiry condition, no similarity or applicability calculus, and no separation of a local quirk from a transferable limitation on independent evidence.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 17-34 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Organisational memory and lessons-learned systems are a required SQ3 adjacent literature and are entirely absent from the anchor set. This omission must be closed; the residual difference is the claim-level unit and the independent target-evidence test.

Citation: B. Chen, J. Tackman, M. Setala, T. Poranen, Z. Zhang, 'Integrating Access Control with Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Proof of Concept for Managing Sensitive Patient Profiles', ACM SAC 2025, pp. 915-919, doi:10.1145/3672608.3707848; B. Chen, T. Taipalus, 'Metadata-aware RAG for Enforcing Access Control and Metadata-based Filtering: Proof of Concept and Evaluation', RACS 2025, pp. 1-7, doi:10.1145/3769002.3769952.
Exact_capability: Enforces fine-grained access control and metadata filtering at the retrieval stage, so that only passages the requesting user is entitled to use can enter the prompt.
What_it_matches: Directly joins similarity retrieval with an authorisation test on the retrieved item - two of the four questions Section 2.4 says a single retrieval step conflates. Entitlement is decided by policy, before augmentation.
What_it_does_not_match: Authorisation is subject-object read permission, not authority to let a prior JUDGMENT act; no currency or validity test on the retrieved item; no applicability appraisal against the target context; no benefit or safety test; both are explicitly proofs of concept, one a five-page short paper.
Evidence: Both DOIs, venues, page ranges and the 2025 year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Requires narrowing of the Section 2.4 statement that retrieval 'carries no test of whether the passage may be used'. That is true of vanilla RAG [58] but no longer true of the 2025 retrieval literature. The residual is currency, applicability and benefit - not authorisation.
Source_verified: YES - Crossref (both); TIER B, proof-of-concept only

Citation: T. Zimmermann, N. Nagappan, H. Gall, E. Giger, B. Murphy, 'Cross-project defect prediction: a large scale experiment on data vs. domain vs. process', ESEC/FSE 2009, pp. 91-100, doi:10.1145/1595696.1595713.
Exact_capability: Large-scale experiment running many cross-project prediction pairs to determine when a defect predictor built on one project transfers to another, and which data, domain and process characteristics govern transfer.
What_it_matches: The closest identified operational analogue to GAP-3's local-versus-transferable distinction: it decides empirically, per source-target pair and against independent TARGET evidence, whether a conclusion learned in one context holds in another, and reports that transfer succeeds only rarely.
What_it_does_not_match: The transferred object is a statistical model fitted to labelled defect data, not one expert's recorded judgment about one contested claim; there is no authorisation, no validity or currency state, no benefit-or-safety gate on the individual reuse event, and the diagnosis concerns predictor portability rather than whether a recurring correction indicates a pipeline limitation or a local quirk.
Evidence: DOI, venue, pages 91-100 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: The strongest challenge to GAP-3's methodological novelty. The proposal must concede that empirical, target-evidence-based transfer testing per source-target pair is established software-engineering practice, and locate its residual in the unit (one recorded human judgment, one reuse event) and in the joint similarity/applicability/authorisation/currency/benefit test.

Candidate_refuter: Relative value of cross-company versus within-company data
Citation: B. Turhan, T. Menzies, A. B. Bener, J. Di Stefano, 'On the relative value of cross-company and within-company data for defect prediction', Empirical Software Engineering 14(5):540-578, 2009, doi:10.1007/s10664-008-9103-7.
Exact_capability: Compares predictors built from other companies' data against predictors built from local data, and introduces nearest-neighbour relevancy filtering of foreign data before reuse.
What_it_matches: Relevancy filtering of foreign experience before it is allowed to act is functionally a similarity-plus-applicability gate on reuse, evaluated against local target outcomes.
What_it_does_not_match: Filtering is by feature-space similarity only; no authorisation, currency or authority; no per-judgment decision; and no explicit quirk-versus-capability-gap classification.
Evidence: DOI, journal, volume, pages 540-578 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Reinforces the Zimmermann narrowing. Cite both as the software-engineering transfer comparators for Study 3.

Citation: J. Nam, S. J. Pan, S. Kim, 'Transfer defect learning', ICSE 2013, pp. 382-391, doi:10.1109/icse.2013.6606584.
Exact_capability: Applies transfer-component analysis with adapted normalisation to make defect predictors transfer across projects with differing feature distributions.
What_it_matches: Demonstrates that transfer requires an explicit adaptation step chosen per source-target pair rather than a copy operation - the same governed-adaptation stance the proposal takes from the guideline literature.
What_it_does_not_match: Adaptation is representational and automatic; no human judgment, authority, currency or reuse authorisation; no diagnostic classification of recurrence.
Evidence: DOI, venue, pages 382-391 and year confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Cite as a transfer-mechanism comparator; less threatening to GAP-3 than Zimmermann, because it assumes transfer is desired rather than deciding whether it is licensed.

Candidate_refuter: Recurrence detection: duplicate defect reports and crash bucketing
Citation: P. Runeson, M. Alexandersson, O. Nyholm, 'Detection of Duplicate Defect Reports Using Natural Language Processing', ICSE 2007, pp. 499-510, doi:10.1109/icse.2007.32; Y. Dang, R. Wu, H. Zhang, D. Zhang, P. Nobel, 'ReBucket: A method for clustering duplicate crash reports based on call stack similarity', ICSE 2012, pp. 1084-1093, doi:10.1109/icse.2012.6227111.
Exact_capability: Detects that a newly reported failure is the same underlying issue as one already recorded, by textual or call-stack similarity, and clusters recurrences.
What_it_matches: Operationalises failure-signature recurrence detection at scale - the detection half of GAP-3's recurrence question, with reported accuracy.
What_it_does_not_match: Establishes only THAT a recurrence is the same issue; performs no diagnostic attribution of the recurrence to a general pipeline limitation versus a local cause, and applies no authorisation, currency or benefit test to reuse.
Evidence: Both DOIs, venues, page ranges and years confirmed via Crossref.
Effect_on_proposal: Cite as the recurrence-detection comparator, so that Study 3's contribution is clearly the diagnostic attribution rather than the detection.
